Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.
2611.25178.title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo

2611.25264.abstract: Printed porous layouts interleave functional material with open channels, and the layout that uses the material best depends on how the process settings shape the deposit. Generative models propose layouts quickly, but a generator that does not receive the process setting samples from the same distribution at every setting, even when the process-dependent score ranks candidate layouts differently. This paper examines whether process knowledge can steer a latent diffusion generator toward layouts suited to a given process setting in a prescribed design domain. We formulate a process-dependent utilization score in which a process model sets the length over which the utility of printed material decays with distance from a channel. The generator combines a vector-quantized variational autoencoder (VQ-VAE) latent representation, a topology U-Net, a ControlNet domain branch, and a separately trained regressor that predicts the score from noised latents; the domain branch conditions each denoising step and the regressor gradient steers it. The method is applied to aerosol jet printing, where the atomizer and sheath gas flows enter the score through the flow-focusing relation. Across seven modeled flow settings, the lowest-scoring candidate layout of a domain differed between settings in 191 of 500 domains. In a sampling study, the mean directly computed score on three validation domains and one test domain was 0.642 with domain conditioning alone, 0.636 at a weight of 300, and 0.450 at 12,000 (112 scores per weight; lower is better). The results support process-knowledge-guided generation as an approach to process-specific porous design under the stated assumptions.
2611.25264.comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables (under review for NAMRC55 - 2027)
2611.25264.title: Process-Knowledge-Guided Latent Diffusion for Generative Design of Porous Architectures: A Case Study in Aerosol Jet Printing

2611.25284.abstract: Hematite is an insulating iron oxide with both a collinear antiferromagnetic and a weakly ferromagnetic phase with intriguing properties, such as long-range spin transport distances, that make it promising for spintronics applications. It has also been identified as a candidate for g-wave altermagnetism. Here, we present the results of fully relativistic ab initio calculations of the magnon properties of hematite, with a focus on altermagnetic effects. We quantitatively evaluate both the anisotropic and altermagnetic magnon band splitting as well as the magnon lifetimes. We show that dipolar interactions lead to a sizeable non-altermagnetic splitting and a hybridisation between opposite-chirality magnons resulting in a strong reduction of the spin expectation value of magnons close to the Γ point and around nodal planes, even in the collinear out-of-plane phase. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.
2611.25284.title: Altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite: from bulk g-wave to planar i-wave

2611.25338.abstract: Generating realistic 3D assets remains constrained by classical representations: surface meshes and compact physically based materials struggle to express objects whose appearance arises from fine geometry or complex light transport, while existing Gaussian-splatting generators typically bake fixed illumination into appearance. We introduce VideoRNG, a two-stage method that generates complete, relightable 3D assets from a text prompt or a single image without prescribing a mesh or analytic material model. A video generator fine-tuned from a pretrained video diffusion backbone first produces a structured RGBA turntable sequence under a known pose, camera, and illumination. A feed-forward large reconstruction model initialized from a pretrained video diffusion backbone then maps the video-VAE latent frames of selected turntable frames directly to millions of anisotropic Gaussians with learned neural appearance features. A shared directional decoder and stochastic Gaussian ray tracer turn this representation, which we call ray-traced Relightable Neural Gaussians (rtRNG), into radiance under novel viewpoints and illumination. To preserve high-frequency appearance while learning geometry, we introduce depth-anchored appearance training, and we make million-Gaussian reconstruction practical through foreground token selection and cost-aware distributed sampling. VideoRNG generates complex assets such as fur, feathers, and spider webs that can be interactively rendered, relit, and integrated into scenes.
2611.25338.title: VideoRNG: Relightable Neural Gaussians from Generative Video Models

2611.25361.abstract: Argumentation frameworks (AFs) provide explicit, formal mechanisms for representing and resolving conflicts and thus have been incorporated into large language model (LLM) decision-making. The benefits vary and depend on how arguments and their relations are constructed, evaluated, and incorporated into the decision process. {We abstract a workflow consisting of four stages based on existing argumentation-augmented methods} and investigate their design choices over tasks of debate-based decision-making and retrieval-based fact verification. Our evaluation with recent LLMs shows that existing methods do not consistently improve performance across the considered tasks. Motivated by this observation, we develop two task-specific methods. The first is called Qnt-Arg, which organizes arguments around the original speakers in debate materials and aggregates model-estimated argument strengths and candidate-answer priors under gradual semantics. The second is Qlt-Arg that uses credibility estimates to establish preferences between conflicting evidence items and applies grounded semantics to select acceptable evidence for subsequent LLM inference. We examine the roles of generative and decision models within the two methods. In the debate setting, Qnt-Arg consistently outperforms other argumentation-augmented methods across matched configurations; Qlt-Arg improves retrieval-based fact-verification performance compared with the baselines. These findings demonstrate the value of combining formal argumentation and LLM while highlighting the importance of aligning with tasks in argumentation construction, model selection, and the role of formal semantic reasoning.
2611.25361.title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation

2611.25375.abstract: Lithium-metal batteries promise high energy density, but common electrolytes trade ionic conductivity against the share of current carried by lithium ions and against how strongly solvent binds those ions. We show that simultaneously weakening both interactions of the lithium ion, with solvent and with anion, relaxes this trade-off. Thus, a weakly coordinating perfluorinated alkoxyaluminate salt in liquefied fluoromethane conducts 39.2 mS cm$^{-1}$ at 25 $^\circ$C while maintaining a lithium-ion transference number of 0.71. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that the anion prevents persistent ion aggregation and lowers the salt's dissociation penalty. Consistent with these properties, nickel-rich cathode/lithium-metal anode full cells charge at 10C at room temperature and at 2C at $-40$ $^\circ$C. We advance coordination strength as a design axis for future energy storage devices.
2611.25375.comment: 12 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to Science. Under review
2611.25375.title: Weakly coordinating anions and solvents break the conductivity-transference-solvation tradeoff

2611.25448.abstract: As fault-tolerant quantum computing emerges, Clifford+T gate basis becomes a popular choice where we need to decompose single-qubit rotation gates into gates in this gate basis. Quantum rotation synthesis may lead to remarkable overhead in quantum circuit compilation. Considering variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) applications as an example, a conventional UCCSD ansatz in quantum chemistry can generate $O(n^4)$ rotations for $n$ qubits. Each optimization iteration updates the rotation angles, making rotation synthesis a recurring cost that can delay the VQE training loop. We identify two sources of delay in rotation synthesis: redundant computation during synthesis and uneven synthesis times that leave workers waiting for slow requests. Atlas addresses these costs with three optimizations: search pruning skips invalid synthesis candidates through statistical inference; adaptive arithmetic avoid unnecessary high-overhead big integer/float arithmetic when decomposing the target rotation gate; batch scheduling fills the gap between the synthesis time of varied rotations. Across various benchmarks, synthesis method, and compilation machines, Atlas can consistently accelerate the rotation synthesis process by up to 12.65x.
2611.25448.title: Atlas: Accelerating Quantum FTQC Compilation with Optimized Algebraic Rotation Synthesis

2611.25452.abstract: Latent crystal generative models typically combine a variational autoencoder (VAE) for learning atom-wise representations with a flow model that transports a simple source distribution to the learned latent distribution. However, previous studies have mainly focused on the quality of generated crystals, leaving the structure and generative utility of the atom-wise latent space largely unexplored. In this work, we show that even a vanilla crystal VAE implicitly organizes atom-wise latent representations according to elemental families, with different families occupying largely separated regions of the latent space. We term this phenomenon emergent chemical semantics. This structure suggests that sampling from a family-specific latent region can bias the decoder toward atoms from the corresponding elemental family. Building on this insight, we propose FamilySpace, a framework for controlling the elemental-family composition of generated crystals. FamilySpace assigns each elemental family a distinct source component, forming a family-indexed multi-source distribution, and trains a flow model using source-target pairs matched by family. In inference, a user-specified family template selects the source component for each atom-wise representation, enabling direct control over the family composition of generated crystals. Experiments on MP-20 and MPTS-52 show that FamilySpace achieves competitive crystal-generation performance while matching prescribed elemental-family compositions. Moreover, selected family templates increase the fraction of generated crystals predicted to be stable or metastable, demonstrating that latent-space composition control can support targeted exploration of promising chemical regions without additional optimization techniques such as reinforcement learning. Code is available at https://github.com/hhw11/FamilySpace
2611.25452.title: FamilySpace: From Emergent Chemical Semantics to Controllable Crystal Generation

2611.25464.abstract: Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development. However, limited attention has been devoted to synthetic time-to-event data, which are central to clinical trials and survival analysis. In particular, theoretical guarantees for the distributional fidelity of synthetic survival data remain largely unexplored. More importantly, even when a generator achieves distributional fidelity, it remains unclear whether the downstream statistical analysis is reliable. To address these gaps, we propose a general two-stage generative framework for survival data (TSGSurv) that jointly generates observed times and covariates conditional on event status, and establish its distributional convergence rate. Focusing on the widely used Cox proportional hazards model, we establish conditions under which generator fidelity guarantees consistency of model coefficient estimates. We further characterize the limitations of naive inference based on synthetic data, and develop a variance correction and a distribution calibration procedure to recover valid inference of original data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed generative and inferential framework with extensive simulations and two real data applications.
2611.25464.title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference

2611.25521.abstract: We present DRVEXO-4B-Unified, a modular multimodal assistant built around a 4B language backbone. A self-contained checkpoint combines text, image, and speech inputs with reference-conditioned speech output and structured interaction. A temporal residual connector adapts acoustic sequences to the language interface; explicit text boundaries support incremental speech synthesis; and three task-conditioned scoring heads rank supplied action candidates alongside generative tool calls. These interfaces connect conversation to application-defined choices while leaving action authorization to the application. The system obtains 74.22% on all 900 MMMU validation questions, exceeding the published validation scores of Gemma 3 4B IT and InternVL3.5-4B without test-time scaling. Strict prompt-level IFEval accuracy is 82.26% and MATH-500 accuracy is 89.40%, above the original Qwen3-4B non-thinking report's 81.2% and 84.8%, respectively. On NVIDIA GB10, the model achieves a speech-synthesis first-chunk latency of 390 ms. For concurrent text generation, a growth-aware admission policy completes a 128-answer batch at 594.41 output tokens/s, including filling and draining, without preemptions. We plan to release the model weights and accompanying code under Apache License 2.0, retaining applicable third-party terms.
2611.25521.title: DRVEXO-4B-Unified: Design and Evaluation of a Modular Speech-Vision System

2611.25577.abstract: Objective: Case investigation and contact tracing are labor-intensive. Web forms struggle when respondents need clarification before disclosing contacts, and open-ended chatbots may deviate from protocols. We developed and evaluated Epira, a protocol-controlled large language model (LLM) interviewer for multi-disease case investigation and contact tracing.   Materials and Methods: Epira pairs LLM dialogue with a rule-based controller enforcing required questions, safety handoffs, and a structured case record, and adapts to new diseases by questionnaire upload. Local (Qwen2.5) and cloud (GPT-5.4) backends were tested. Study 1 used 108 simulated cases with ground-truth fields and contacts for measles and gonorrhea under Epira and open-ended conditions (864 sessions). Study 2 enrolled 72 volunteers in a 2$\times$2 disease-by-model interview assessing completion, usability, acceptability, and trust.   Results: Across Study 1, Epira with a local LLM captured 88.9% of required fields and 60.1% of ground-truth contacts. Open-ended interviewers recovered 31.1-41.9 percentage points fewer required fields than the same models in Epira. In Study 2, completion was 100%; mean adapted System Usability Scale (SUS) was 82.95 $\pm$ 16.17 on a 0-100 scale and mean trust was 3.85 $\pm$ 0.77 on a 1-5 scale.   Discussion: Protocol control drove completeness more than model choice. Local and cloud deployments produced similar records, supporting privacy-preserving local use with human review of routed interviews and missed contacts.   Conclusion: Epira recovers required fields and contacts under diverse disclosure conditions, works with local and cloud LLMs, and received favorable usability and trust ratings.
2611.25577.title: Design and Evaluation of Epira: An Automated Interview System for Case Investigation and Contact Tracing

2611.25646.abstract: Fast and accurate prediction of adsorption energies is critical for high-throughput computational catalyst screening, existing methods compromise either on evaluation speed (full-graph machine learning potentials) or geometric sensitivity (coordination-based models like the alpha-scheme). Here, we present AdsNet, an equivariant graph neural network that directly predicts adsorption energies in a single forward pass, which operates on a local graph restricted only to adsorbate atoms and its immediate surface neighbors within a cutoff radius. This local graph formulation decouples computational complexity from total system size while encoding continuous geometric features (interatomic distances and directional vectors) enabling sensitivity to subtle variations in local bonding environments. AdsNet adopts a message-passing architecture with scalar and vector node features over multiple interaction layers. Trained on AdsTraj, a dataset of 33,920 density functional theory (DFT) calculated structures spanning 26 transition metals and 6 adsorbates (H*, C*, O*, CO*, OH*, HOCO*), the model achieves an adsorption energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.032 eV and a force RMSE of 0.047 eV/A. Analytic forces obtained via automatic differentiation enable structure relaxation through a projected gradient descent algorithm with adaptive line search, eliminating entire geometry optimizations. Additionally, AdsNet uniquely decomposes predicted adsorption energies into contributions from individual atoms within the local adsorbate graph - an interpretability feature unattainable with conventional machine-learning potentials. AdsNet thus establishes an accurate, highly efficient, and interpretable framework for large-scale adsorption energy prediction and local interface relaxation across various material surfaces.
2611.25646.comment: 24 pages, 6 figures, 1 table; includes Supplementary Information (4 pages, 2 tables). AdsNet is MIT-licensed. Code: https://github.com/changzhiai/AdsNet - Documentation: https://adsnet.readthedocs.io - Dataset (AdsTraj): https://huggingface.co/datasets/changzhiai/AdsTraj - Model weights: https://huggingface.co/changzhiai/adsnet-models
2611.25646.title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction

2611.25651.abstract: Materials science involves highly heterogeneous scientific information, including textual knowledge, molecular and crystal structures, experimental characterization data, microscopy images, and structure-property relationships. Developing a general-purpose foundation model capable of understanding and reasoning over these diverse materials representations remains challenging. In this technical report, we introduce MatVerse, a materials foundation model built upon Intern-S2-Preview and further specialized through large-scale materials-domain post-training. We construct a large-scale multimodal training corpus covering materials knowledge, scientific reasoning, quantitative problem solving, structural understanding, and multimodal scientific interpretation. To improve domain adaptation, we develop a unified data construction pipeline combining teacher-guided reasoning distillation, scientific problem synthesis, consistency-based filtering, and retrieval-based multimodal data construction. We evaluate MatVerse on three representative materials-science benchmarks: our human-calibrated OmniMatBench, MatSciBench, and MaCBench. Results demonstrate consistent improvements after materials-specific post-training over the base model on all three benchmarks, alongside improved inference efficiency on calculation-intensive problems. These results show that targeted domain-specific post-training can effectively enhance scientific reasoning, materials knowledge understanding, and multimodal scientific capabilities of foundation models. MatVerse provides a unified language-and-vision interface for materials science and serves as a foundation for future AI-assisted materials research workflows.
2611.25651.title: MatVerse: A Foundation Model for Materials Science

2611.25661.abstract: Large Language Models show great potential for automated Register-Transfer Level repair, yet they struggle with non-local faults where root causes and failing outputs reside far apart in source code. Treating RTL as a flat token sequence obscures hardware dataflows, whereas exposing complete synthesized graphs overwhelms the model with fine-grained metadata. To resolve this representation dilemma, we propose GRODE-RTL, an anchor-centric representation that extracts the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, maps netlist nodes back to editable source lines, and organizes them into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. By prioritizing direct drivers and folding distant hops, GRODE-RTL guides standard tool-using agents without exposing ground-truth hints or oracle feedback. We evaluate GRODE-RTL across 30 formally validated non-local faults using three LLMs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.2, and MiniMax-M3) alongside a controlled six-configuration ablation study. GRODE-RTL improves pass@1 over source-level exploration by 16.7% on DeepSeek, by 26.7% on GLM-5.2, and by 20.0% on MiniMax-M3, with consistent gains on the hard-to-retrieve far-distance and indirect-anchor subsets of all three models. Our controls isolate structural relevance from generic context expansion, proving that selective dependency organization rather than full graph exposure is key to effective RTL repair.
2611.25661.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair

2611.25750.abstract: Ice-cloud retrievals from polarimetric radar, lidar and submillimeter radiometry commonly assume random orientation, horizontal alignment or a prescribed flutter angle. We link the orientation dynamics of ice crystals to their scattering. Fluid-inertial torque turns small settling crystals broadside on, and turbulent velocity gradients turn them away, so their orientation depends on the dissipation rate. We combine a closed-form orientation distribution for overdamped spheroids, including rotational diffusion and turbulence intermittency, with orientation-averaged Rayleigh, Rayleigh--Gans, T-matrix and specular scattering. Turbulence enters the scattering only through the Legendre moments of the orientation distribution. In the Rayleigh regime the specific differential phase follows crystal alignment, so assuming perfectly horizontal crystals biases ice-water-content retrievals low. Combining the specific differential phase with differential reflectivity limits this bias to $25\%$ for a single size of the shapes studied. For size distributions that span the alignment transition the bound can fail, because the two observables weight sizes differently. Depolarization adds sensitivity to higher-order moments and to intermittency. At finite size the second orientation moment mainly controls the scattering cross sections and the asymmetry parameter, and for optically soft crystals its contribution vanishes $54.7^\circ$ from the vertical. Specular returns from partly aligned plates should persist for lidars pointed $3^\circ$ from nadir. An exploratory analysis of EarthCARE lidar data finds a weakly depolarizing, low-lidar-ratio signature most frequent near $-11^\circ$C, where plates grow. Degree-scale tilt widths inferred from glints and lidar require larger crystals, near or beyond the validity range of the model.
2611.25750.title: Scattering by Small Ice Crystals in Turbulence: From Orientation Statistics to Retrieval Biases

2611.25779.abstract: The ability to measure thermal properties and visualize heat transport processes with high spatial resolution is becoming increasingly important for materials discovery, next-generation electronics, and advanced manufacturing. As critical dimensions and architectures of novel materials and high performance electronics shrink and become more heterogeneous, thermal transport is no longer governed by bulk material properties alone, but by local variations in microstructure, such as interfaces and defects, while the operating conditions can also play a role. With the development of non-contact pump-probe thermoreflectance techniques, specific heat, thermal conductivity, and interface conductance can be mapped either through wide-field thermos-reflectance images or by scanning technique. However, key challenges remain such as the balance between imaging throughput and measurement accuracy, the extraction of multiple parameters with high confidence, and non-intrusive subsurface characterization, etc. This Review highlights recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI)-assistance in high-throughput data processing, visualizing interfacial thermal transport, and nonintrusive subsurface analysis, and offers outlooks for future research directions such as spectral mapping of heat carriers, three-dimensional property mapping, and AI-agentic experimental designs. We anticipate this Review will motivate future efforts in combining AI with experimental techniques to achieve unprecedented capabilities for thermal characterization of nanoscale materials and device characterization, facilitating materials discovery and electronics revolution.
2611.25779.title: Intelligent Imaging of Thermal Transport in Nanostructures

2611.25836.abstract: Molecular dynamics simulation of the solidification behavior of an AlCoCuFeNi high-entropy alloy nanowire was performed using an embedded atom model potential at cooling rates of 10^11, 10^12, and 10^13 K/s. Periodic boundary conditions were applied along the nanowire axis to model an effectively infinite nanowire. The crystallization process was characterized through the temperature dependence of the potential energy. Structural evolution was analyzed using adaptive common-neighbor analysis (CNA) and radial distribution functions (RDF). The results show that the final structure changes from amorphous to crystalline with decreasing cooling rate, demonstrating the strong influence of cooling conditions on phase formation in nanoscale high-entropy alloy systems.
2611.25836.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation of the Solidification of AlCoCuFeNi High-Entropy Alloy Nanowire

2611.25899.abstract: Background: In nucleon-induced fission up to GeV energies, early nonequilibrium emission alters the residual nuclei before statistical evaporation and scission. The emitted light particles therefore probe each reaction stage while supplying needed nuclear data.   Purpose: We study neutron and light charged-particle emission in $^{235,238}$U$(n,f)$ and $^{235,238}$U$(p,f)$ reactions at incident energies from 10 MeV to 1 GeV.   Methods: The reactions are simulated event by event by coupling the isospin-dependent quantum molecular dynamics model with the GEMINI++ statistical decay code.   Results: The calculations follow the measured rise in average neutron multiplicity with incident energy, while yielding higher values above 100 MeV and in the proton-induced prescission component. Within the coupled calculations, the neutron multiplicity growth comes mainly from statistical evaporation before scission, whereas emission from the fission fragments changes weakly. Although the average preequilibrium neutron yield remains small, early emission spreads the residual nuclei across multiple elements and wide excitation energies. At high energies, protons are emitted predominantly before equilibration, directly reducing the charge retained by the residual nuclei.   Conclusions: In the coupled calculations, statistical evaporation before scission governs the neutron multiplicity growth, whereas early nonequilibrium emission shapes the residual nuclei and dominates high-energy proton emission. These results provide a reference for modeling intermediate-energy fission, in which prescission emission changes the charge, mass, and excitation energy of the fissioning system.
2611.25899.title: Light-particle emission in nucleon-induced fission of $^{235,238}$U at energies from 10 MeV to 1 GeV

2611.25907.abstract: In this paper we present a systematic first-principles investigation of the structure and nearest-neighbor magnetic exchange interactions in the infinite-layer RNiO2 thin-film series (R = La-Lu), under the constrain of different substrates. Density functional theory calculations are first employed to optimize the crystal structures, while CAS+DDCI correlated wave-function calculations were used for the determination of the magnetic exchanges. This methodology allows to obtain magnetic interactions in good agreement with RIXS experimental estimations. In the pristine case, our results confirm that the structure of RNiO2 (except for R = La and Ce) adopts the I4/mcm space group, characterized by an out-of-plane rotation of the NiO4 plaquettes. This result remains valid under substrate constrains, even if compressive strain reduces the amplitude of the rotational distortion and leads to an enhancement of the magnetic exchange interaction relative to the pristine structures. The latter are found to depend sensitively on both the rare-earth ionic radius and the applied epitaxial strain. These results highlight the role of structural distortions and substrate-induced strain in tuning magnetic interactions in infinite-layer nickelates.
2611.25907.title: Ab-initio study of magnetic interaction in RNiO2: role of rare-earth size and epitaxial strain

2611.25928.abstract: In this work, we investigate thermal transport in a set of thin-film layers used in modern HEMT designs. Our theoretical analysis employs three phonon-transport models of increasing sophistication, ranging from a relatively simple Debye-approximation model to a first-principles framework that incorporates Density Functional Theory (DFT)-derived harmonic and anharmonic phonon properties. To describe ternary semiconductors, alloy scattering is also considered, and to account for the properties of non-ideal, polycrystalline thin films, scattering at grain and film boundaries is taken into account. For modeling the specific samples at hand, the latter are fitted to thermal conductivity data measured with Time-Domain Thermoreflectance (TDTR). Overall, we find that the first-principles model performs best and produces the most physically consistent results. Special emphasis is placed on establishing a reliable procedure for determining intrinsic transport properties dominated by Umklapp scattering. Building on these, it is then possible to systematically add additional scattering terms to the models and assess how model-inherent factors, such as the treatment of scattering rates or the description of the phonon dispersion, affect model accuracy and overall predictive capabilities.
2611.25928.title: Thermal investigation of buffer and transition layers in AlGaN HEMT stacks

2611.25944.abstract: Grain boundaries (GBs) in polycrystalline Ni-based alloys strongly influence mechanical strength and fracture behavior, yet the effect of alloying elements such as Fe and Cr on GB cohesion remains difficult to quantify systematically. Using density functional theory (DFT), we compute rigid-body separation (RBS) curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni GBs, extracting the work of separation $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and maximum traction $σ_{\max}$ via the universal binding energy relation (UBER). We find that substitution of Cr or Fe into the GB plane increases both quantities relative to pure Ni GBs. To overcome the size limitations of DFT, we compare several machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP) foundation models against the DFT dataset and identify a model achieving quantitative agreement with DFT for $W_{\mathrm{sep}}$ and $σ_{\max}$. This MLIP enables systematic sampling of alloying configurations at finer concentration steps. We show that alloying-induced changes in GB cohesion depend on both, element type and local structures, revealing trends that are inaccessible with DFT alone. Extending the analysis to a ternary $\mathrm{Ni}_{56}\mathrm{Fe}_{20}\mathrm{Cr}_{24}$ composition, inspired by the principal constituents of the widely used commercial Alloy 718, shows that the binary trends provide a useful basis for interpreting the combined effect of both substitutes, while explicit ternary calculations are required to capture their interplay quantitatively. Together, these results provide a validated workflow for quantifying the effect of alloying elements on GB cohesion in multicomponent alloys. The resulting values may serve as input for continuum-scale fracture models, paving the way toward atomistically informed multiscale modeling.
2611.25944.title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system

2611.26183.abstract: Over the past three centuries, many thermodynamics researchers have worked to develop fluid equations of state with both high accuracy and broad applicability, proposing various theoretical frameworks and models. Building on these efforts, this study uses Gibbs free energy as the starting point and introduces thermodynamically consistent neural networks to construct a fluid equation of state based on Gibbs free energy (GEoS). This approach establishes a novel machine learning framework that provides a unified representation of fluid states. GEoS performs well on the vapor- and liquid-phase density test sets, with average absolute relative deviations (AARDs) of 5.25% and 3.96%, respectively. It outperforms conventional volume-translated cubic equations of state and existing machine learning models, demonstrating its effectiveness. Further analysis using the UMAP dimensionality reduction method shows that most molecules in the test set belong to extrapolation systems, confirming the strong generalization ability of the model. Finally, the test results show that the PC-SAFT equation fitted using GEoS maintains high predictive accuracy, providing a reliable basis for its practical application in industry.
2611.26183.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Neural Networks for a Universal Fluid Gibbs Free Energy Equation of State

2611.26186.abstract: Reward misalignment is usually regarded as a failure of artificial intelligence. In materials discovery with generative AI models, however, disagreement between predefined rewards and expert judgment may reveal materials that the rewards overlook. We investigate this possibility using electronic flat bands as a prime example. Experts mostly agree with a numerical bandwidth score, but their disagreements are systematic and cannot be explained by an estimated 5% rate of mistaken labels. We learn the experts' preferences from pairwise comparisons and use them to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and numerical score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere. For example, the preferences favor KCo2As2 and CoGa, reported compounds with partially flat bands that the score would discard. The framework also extends to synthesizability and phonon properties. Our findings suggest that reward misalignment can expose opportunities for materials discovery beyond what fixed rewards are designed to find.
2611.26186.comment: 33 pages (15 pages main text and 18 pages Supplementary Information), 4 figures
2611.26186.title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery

2611.26233.abstract: We present three global adiabatic potential energy surfaces (PESs) for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$, a $^3Π_u$) to CO(X$^1Σ^+$) + C($^3$P) reaction, computed at the icMRCI+Q/aug-cc-pVTZ level. This reaction is relevant to combustion chemistry, atmospheric processes, and astrochemistry. Since the energy difference between the $^1Σ_g^+$ and $^3Π_u$ states of C$_2$ is smaller than the zero-point energy, both states mix upon interaction with the approaching O atom. Consequently, the PESs exhibit a double-well topography in the reactant valley. Beyond this feature, the three PESs display markedly different topographies. The 1 $^3A''$ PES features a deep minimum 7.16 eV below the O + C$_2$ entrance channel. In contrast, the 2 $^3A''$ and 1 $^3A'$ surfaces possess shallower collinear wells ($\approx$ 5.7 eV) and strong angular anisotropy arising from avoided crossings with higher-lying triplet states. The analytical fits reproduce the \textit{ab initio} data with root-mean-square (RMS) deviations of 0.022--0.028 eV over an energy interval exceeding 13 eV. Quasiclassical trajectory (QCT) calculations reveal higher reactivity on the barrierless $1\,^3A''$ surface compared to the $2\,^3A''$ PES, where an angle-dependent entrance barrier reduces the cross sections. Furthermore, cross sections for reactions initiated from C$_2$(X $^1Σ_g^+$) and C$_2$(a $^3Π_u$) are remarkably similar for the three PESs, regardless of the initial rovibrational state.
2611.26233.comment: 15 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to Journal of Chemical Physics
2611.26233.title: Triplet adiabatic potential energy surfaces for the O($^3$P) + C$_2$(X$^1Σ_g^+$, a$^3Π_u$) reaction and quasiclassical trajectory dynamics

2611.26349.abstract: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores. The agent turns natural-language requests into relaxation-to-band workflows, from a single uploaded structure to automatically constructed new candidates and returns predicted properties.
2611.26349.title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation

2611.26359.abstract: Continuous diffusion models generate discrete data through stochastic dynamics in an embedding space. We consider jump diffusions that additionally reset coordinates to embeddings of categorical values. A coordinate's own corrupted state can make prediction easy, potentially reducing the pressure to learn dependencies between coordinates. We study leave-one-out (LOO) prediction, in which each coordinate is predicted from the corrupted states of the other coordinates. We show that, under stated assumptions, jump diffusions with complete coordinate resets and state-independent clocks preserve the prescribed marginals when reset destinations use exact LOO probabilities and the drift uses the full endpoint posterior. We further show that this drift can be constructed from LOO probabilities by analytic likelihood completion without additional network evaluations. We evaluate unrestricted, LOO, and completed predictions on Text8 and LM1B text generation and ZINC250k molecular graph generation. LOO-based variants improve key generation metrics over matched unrestricted controls on all three datasets. Controlled interventions assess reliance on local inputs and context, and we analyze the effect of analytic likelihood completion.
2611.26359.title: Learning from Context: Leave-One-Out Prediction in Jump Diffusions

2611.26404.abstract: The interpretation of nuclear levels in experiments and ab initio computations is challenging because it requires the production and analysis of many expectation values and transition strengths. Here we introduce an approach that yields directly interpretable states. Our ab initio coupled-cluster computations start from a reference state with axial symmetry and positive parity. Equation-of-motion techniques then yield intrinsic states with definite parity and angular-momentum projection onto the symmetry axis. Finally, the projection onto good angular momenta yields rotational bands based on these intrinsic states. In the neutron-rich nucleus $^{34}$Mg, where only the ground-state band is known, we find several low-lying positive- and negative-parity bands. The lowest, a $K^π=3^-$ band, is dominated by a single neutron particle-hole excitation rather than by octupole collectivity. These results challenge the common wisdom about how deformation and pairing work in nuclei.
2611.26404.title: Interpretation follows computation for deformed atomic nuclei

2611.26533.abstract: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.
2611.26533.title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials

2611.26550.abstract: Mapping the distribution of elements in the Milky Way and understanding how that distribution has changed over time can give us insight into the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. Here we use homogeneously estimated atmospheric parameters, elemental abundances, distances, and ages for ~580,000 giants from five major spectroscopic surveys---all simultaneously placed on a single, self-consistent scale by one model---allowing us, for the first time, to use a large sample of stars with uniform labels and ages that cumulatively span much of the disk to trace how the metallicity structure of the Milky Way depends on stellar age. Our chrono-chemical analysis shows that the radial metallicity gradient of the disk depends non-monotonically on age: it is shallow for the youngest stars, steepening to a maximum of ~-0.07 dex/kpc at intermediate ages (~5-6 Gyr), and flattening to near zero for the oldest stars. This "U-shaped" age dependence is driven largely by the low-alpha (thin-disk) population, with the high-alpha (thick-disk) sequence having weak gradients at all ages. In contrast to [Fe/H], the radial [Mg/Fe] gradient is weak (<~0.01 dex/kpc) at all ages. Together, these trends are consistent with an inside-out formation scenario in which the gradient of the star-forming gas has flattened over at least the last ~6 Gyr, while the near-zero gradient of the oldest stars reflects their formation in a well-mixed disk, efficient radial migration, or both.
2611.26550.comment: 20 pages, 17 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to ApJ
2611.26550.title: Chemical Cartography Across Time: The Age-Dependent Chemical Structure of the Milky Way with a Homogeneous Sample of 580,000 Giants from Five Surveys

2611.26717.abstract: Synthesizing relational training data such as knowledge graphs with a large language model typically emits structured objects one at a time, which keeps each object valid but leaves the relationships between them ungrounded. We study an alternative paradigm, generation by simulation: rather than describing a relational artifact, we simulate a process that produces it and take the artifact to be its causal record. Language-model agents propose intent and a deterministic referee resolves outcomes against an explicit world model, so a relation is emitted only when the event it represents occurs, making coherence a property of construction. We instantiate the paradigm for cyber threat intelligence knowledge graphs in the STIX 2.1 standard with three engines, among them an evolutionary engine applying language-model genetic operators to structured graph genomes, sharing a deterministic compiler that makes malformed and dangling output unrepresentable. We prove referential closure, causal grounding, and identifier stability, an ablation localizes each to the referee and world model rather than the policy, and two independent LLM judges reproduce the rubric's engine ranking. Our central result is cautionary, and we prove it: a validator reading any graph feature set a structure-matched random graph can reproduce is uninformative about coherence for a coherence-by-construction generator. Using Erdős-Rényi controls we realize the theorem four times, as structural separation, embedding transfer, inductive link prediction, and real-data augmentation each reward a triviality rather than coherence; we give the mechanism behind each and the conditions a valid benchmark must meet.
2611.26717.comment: 21 pages, 5 figures. Includes supplementary material (Sections S-I through S-X)
2611.26717.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation

2611.26724.abstract: We investigate cavity-controlled hysteresis and multilevel molecular switching in a hybrid molecular optomechanical system composed of a plasmonic nanocavity, a Fabry-Pérot cavity, and an ensemble of molecular vibrations. Molecular-plasmonic optomechanical interaction together with cavity-plasmon hybridization produce bistability and dynamical hysteresis, leading to a history-dependent optical and molecular response. An analytical treatment of the steady-state equations shows that the auxiliary cavity renormalizes the effective optical linewidth and detuning, while the collective molecular interaction generates an effective nonlinearity. Together, these effects enable control of the hysteretic regime through optical detuning, cavity-plasmon coupling, and molecular ensemble size. Beyond bistability, pulsed excitation generates staircase-like molecular dynamics, with ascending or descending vibrational populations depending on the optical driving configuration. In particular, the FP cavity controls the buildup of vibrational excitation, while simultaneous driving of both optical modes enables stepwise vibrational depletion. These results establish hybrid molecular optomechanical systems as a tunable platform for history-dependent and pulse-driven molecular dynamics, with potential applications in nanoscale memory, multilevel information processing, and optically controlled molecular switching.
2611.26724.title: Cavity-Controlled Hysteresis and Multilevel Molecular Switching in Hybrid Optomechanics

2611.26782.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. Yet an MD study requires an expert-driven workflow: designing the simulation, writing reliable input scripts, executing them, and analyzing the results with separate tools. Here we present ChatAtom, a multi-agent large language model system that translates a natural-language request into a complete MD workflow without the user writing input scripts or analysis code. Each agent has a defined responsibility within the workflow. An orchestrator plans the study; the LAMMPS and OVITO agents each use a generator-reviewer pair to prepare and review simulation and visualization scripts before execution; a high-performance computing agent dispatches jobs to remote resources; and an analysis agent interprets the completed run. The work- flow is accessible through a browser interface that streams thermodynamic data and rendered frames during local execution, allowing users to follow the simu- lation as it progresses. The architecture also supports new capabilities through loadable skills without modifying the agents, enabling autonomous hypothesis generation and testing. We evaluate ChatAtom through script-generation bench- marks, an end-to-end study of crack propagation, and a closed-loop campaign. By bringing script generation, execution, visualization, and analysis into one reviewed and observable pipeline, ChatAtom lowers the barrier to conducting MD studies and broadens access to advanced simulation workflows.
2611.26782.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization

2611.26819.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate the potential energy surface of atomistic systems from quantum-mechanical reference data and enable molecular simulation at near-ab-initio accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Since they are fitted to total energies and forces, it is not obvious what is estimated: the total energy or the many-body potentials from which it is assembled. Mathematically, this can be formulated as a question whether a function can be recovered from averages of its values over random clusters. We study it for a linear model of fixed correlation order in simplified statistical setting. We show that, in the population limit, the potential is identifiable in a natural weighted Sobolev space, and derive finite-sample recovery guarantees. Numerical experiments for pair, three-body, and four-body models support the theory.
2611.26819.title: Recovering from Averages: An Inverse Problem Perspective on Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials

2611.26892.abstract: Helical polypeptides combine the chemical tunability of synthetic macromolecules with the highly ordered backbone architecture of natural proteins. Here, density-functional tight-binding calculations are used to determine how chain length and sequence chemistry govern the dipolar and electronic properties of three $α$-helical polypeptide families: polyalanine [AAAAA]$_n$, leucine-modified [AAAAL]$_n$, and cysteine-capped, lysine-containing C[AAAAK]$_n$. Increasing chain length produces systematic shifts and splitting of the molecular orbital levels together with an approximately additive increase in the molecular dipole. Analysis of the C[AAAAK]$_3$ helix shows that aligned backbone carbonyl groups provide the dominant contribution to the macro dipole, whose growing electrostatic potential is consistent with an intrinsic Stark-like contribution to the length-dependent orbital-energy evolution. Side-chain and terminal modifications introduce localized perturbations to frontier electronic states while preserving this global backbone-driven trend. Residue-resolved frontier levels additionally form a staircase-like energy landscape along the helical scaffold: individual peptide units retain large local HOMO-LUMO gaps of approximately 5 eV, whereas spatially proximate hydrogen-bonded residues exhibit smaller inter-residue energy separations. Application of external electrostatic fields modifies the frontier-level separation in a direction-dependent manner and induces structural distortions predominantly near the flexible termini, while the helical core remains comparatively robust. By establishing these fundamental sequence-structure-property relationships, this work provides a foundational blueprint for the rational design of peptide-based biomacromolecules tailored for next-generation bio-electronic interfaces, biosensors, and artificial electron-transfer systems.
2611.26892.comment: Manuscript: 19 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables; SI: 6 pages, 6 figures, 2 table
2611.26892.title: Length and Sequence-Dependent Dipolar and Electronic Properties of $α$-helical Polypeptides

2611.27015.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery proceeds through repeated design-make-test-analyze cycles. The goal is often to maximize potency while keeping other properties within the ranges required for a viable therapeutic candidate. Compound prioritization places different demands on computational methods as drug discovery progresses from hit identification through hit-to-lead and lead optimization, with changing computational budgets and increasing amounts of on-target experimental data. We introduce Ruby, a Robust Universal Binding affinitY predictor that uses intermediate representations from the structural foundation model Pearl without requiring an explicit binding pose for every compound. Ruby is trained on proprietary data plus GenesisPotency-2026, an audited public-source potency training dataset released for academic and commercial use under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license with row-level provenance and audit annotations. Ruby achieves the highest aggregate early enrichment across seven public hit-identification targets among evaluated methods, with adjustable inference effort trading off enrichment and computational cost over more than two orders of magnitude. Ruby achieves the highest average correlations across four public benchmarks: OpenFE, CASP16, FEP+ 4, and OpenBind. Ruby significantly outperforms other methods in zero-shot prediction across eight biochemical and cellular assays from five ongoing Genesis-Incyte programs, widening its performance advantage relative to the public benchmarks. Ruby continues to improve more than other methods when all are given the opportunity to recalibrate using earlier assay measurements. Together, these contributions provide an annotated training resource for the field and a state-of-the-art potency predictor for broad screening, prioritization within related chemical series, and assay-specific prediction as experimental measurements accumulate.
2611.27015.title: Ruby: State-of-the-Art Potency Prediction across Discovery Regimes Using Learned Structural Representations

2611.27017.abstract: Wilderness search-and-rescue (WSAR) teams use uncrewed aerial systems (UASs) to survey terrain for indicators of missing persons that are rare, blend into the background, or lack thermal signatures. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) provides rich spectral information, but its high data volume challenges real-time on-drone processing. We present SABL, an edge-computing pipeline for on-drone Spectral Anomaly-Based Localization. SABL integrates hyperspectral streaming with exponentially moving Reed-Xiaoli (ERX) anomaly detection and DBSCAN spatial filtering to group pixel-level anomalies into candidate search regions. SABL is evaluated on data collected during a 10-day deployment with Quinhagak Search and Rescue (QSAR) in remote Alaska. It processes hyperspectral scanlines at 5.67-5.73 ms per line, meeting the camera's 10-ms acquisition interval; DBSCAN requires only 6.5-12.5 ms per 100-line update for filtering. SABL achieves approximately 56% and 99% object-level precision on QSAR-selected search indicators across two scenes, with corresponding recall of 55% and 29%, providing significant background filtering while identifying difficult-to-see anomalous search indicators.
2611.27017.title: Real-Time On-Drone Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection for Wilderness Search and Rescue

2611.27037.abstract: Hybrid density functional theory calculations were used to investigate the stability, electronic properties, and catalytic activity of transition-metal impurities substituting Zn sites (M\(_{\rm Zn}\)) in the MOF-5 metal-organic framework [Zn\(_4\)O(BDC)\(_3\), BDC = 1,4-benzenedicarboxylate], with M = Sc, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu. Most substitutions introduce \(3d\) states within the MOF-5 band gap and induce localized magnetic moments. Partially occupied \(3d\) states promote orbital hybridization and charge transfer with oxygenated intermediates, activating the dopant sites toward oxygen electrocatalysis. The oxygen reduction and evolution reaction (ORR and OER) activities were evaluated using the computational hydrogen electrode model. Mn\(_{\rm Zn}\) and Fe\(_{\rm Zn}\) exhibit calculated ORR overpotentials of 0.57~V, while Mn\(_{\rm Zn}\) and Co\(_{\rm Zn}\) yield OER overpotentials of 0.42 and 0.51~V, respectively, approaching those of benchmark precious-metal electrocatalysts. These findings identify Mn substitution as a promising strategy for achieving bifunctional ORR/OER activity in MOF-5 and establish a link between dopant electronic structure and catalytic performance to guide the design of MOF-based electrocatalysts.
2611.27037.title: Transition-Metal Substitutions in MOF-5: A Hybrid-DFT Study of Oxygen Electrocatalysis

2611.27058.abstract: Co-folding models predict the structures of proteins and their bound ligands, but their accuracy varies across targets. Their usefulness therefore depends on knowing which predictions a user can trust. Confidence scores are intended to guide that choice. However, across seven co-folding models, we show that confidence-based selection offers little improvement over choosing a prediction at random. For approximately three-quarters of structures, predictions are either exclusively correct or incorrect, leaving no opportunity for ranking to change the outcome. Moreover, high confidence does not reliably discriminate correct top-ranked predictions from incorrect ones. We find that structural agreement among predictions is a more accurate measure of likely success than current confidence scores. We capture this with the Concentration of Repeated Ensembles (CORE) Score, which combines cluster tightness with ensemble support. CORE Score discriminates top-1 success and oracle success, achieving mean ROC AUCs of 0.866 and 0.838, compared to 0.757 and 0.759 for ipTM. CORE Score also outperforms training set similarity measures, including ligand Tanimoto, protein sequence, and Runs N' Poses similarity, despite requiring no experimental ligand pose. Structural agreement is therefore a practical indicator of reliability and a baseline for evaluating future confidence estimators, without requiring an additional trained uncertainty estimator.
2611.27058.comment: 30 pages, 9 figures, 20 supplementary figures, 3 supplementary tables. Code: https://github.com/oxpig/core-score
2611.27058.title: Structural Agreement Indicates Prediction Accuracy For Protein-Ligand Co-Folding

2611.27063.abstract: Video fusion integrates complementary information in multiple source video streams into a single sequence for complete scene perception. Existing methods perform frame-wise fusion and lack unified spatio-temporal modeling across sequences, damaging temporal coherence across sequences. When dealing with degradations, they also ignore temporal dynamics and overload a single network with diverse degradations, leading to limited and imbalanced degradation suppression. To address these issues, we propose V2VFusion, the first unified video-to-video fusion framework that directly generates temporally coherent, high-quality fused videos from degraded multi-source inputs. By reformulating video fusion as a video-to-video conditional generation problem in latent diffusion space, our approach holistically models spatio-temporal dependencies across entire sequences and intrinsically ensures sequence-level consistency. On this basis, a text-guided degradation-conditioned ControlNet bridges high-level textual degradation descriptions with low-level visual priors, enabling interpretable and controllable guidance for structure-preserving fusion beyond purely data-driven conditioning. To handle heterogeneous and compound degradations, a state-modulated degradation-aware hierarchical mixture-of-experts module decouples expert selection into diffusion-state-aware filtering and degradation-aware routing. It prevents unreliable routing and fosters expert specialization to mitigate representation conflicts among diverse degradations. Experiments on infrared-visible, multi-exposure, and multi-focus video fusion tasks and complex degradations validate that V2VFusion surpasses existing methods in fusion quality and temporal stability. The code is available at https://github.com/ChenDoubleJ/V2VFusion.
2611.27063.title: V2VFusion: Text-Controlled Video-to-Video Diffusion for Degradation-Aware Video Fusion

2611.27103.abstract: Transition metal chalcogenide M6X6 nanowires (M = Mo or W; X = S, Se, or Te) are promising one-dimensional (1D) building blocks for nanowire bundles and arrays, but how elemental composition controls their intrinsic axial heat transport remains unclear. Here we develop a multicomponent neuroevolution potential (NEP) from first-principles reference data and use homogeneous nonequilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations to quantify the thermal conductivity of six MX6 nanowires. The Mo6X6 series show a nonmonotonic composition dependence, whereas the thermal conductivity of the W6X6 series decreases monotonically with increasing chalcogen mass. Frequency-resolved thermal conductivity and phonon mean-free path analyses show that axial heat conduction is dominated by low-frequency phonons. Vibrational density of states and spectral energy density analyses further reveal that the contrasting trends arise from a competition between metal-chalcogen vibrational matching and phonon softening induced by heavier chalcogen atoms. A phenomenological model incorporating the combined atomic mass and the relative mass difference between the metal and chalcogen atoms reproduces these trends. These results link elemental composition, phonon characteristics and axial thermal conductivity in M6X6 nanowires, providing an atomistic basis for selecting heat-conducting units in nanowire bundles and arrays.
2611.27103.title: Axial Thermal Transport in Transition Metal Chalcogenide Nanowires from Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Simulations

2611.27162.abstract: Predicting holo-like protein conformations from apo structures is essential in structure-based drug design. Most existing apo-to-holo models operate in Cartesian space and achieve strong global accuracy. However, high global accuracy does not ensure physically valid local backbone geometry. Internal-coordinate models offer local control and validity, but regressive generation can amplify angular errors, known as the lever-arm effect. We introduce CrypticFlow, a hierarchical flow-matching model that combines these two complementary representations. An ESM-3-conditioned E(3)-equivariant graph network first generates sparse C$α$ anchors in Cartesian space. A conditional midpoint Transformer then recursively fills the gaps in local internal coordinates. During recursive generation, the decoder constrains the distance between each midpoint and any sequence-adjacent parent anchor to the corresponding apo C$α$-C$α$ distance. On the D3PM test split, CrypticFlow achieves the lowest median and mean C$α$ RMSD at published baseline capacities. Across five independent training models, the median and mean direct RMSD are 1.333 $\pm$ 0.056 angstroms and 2.766 $\pm$ 0.041 angstroms, respectively. The quality of local geometry also improves substantially. Our model achieves 99.58 $\pm$ 0.02% adjacent-distance fidelity and 95.87 $\pm$ 0.25% pseudo-angle fidelity, measured within 0.2 angstroms and 20° of the holo reference. Then, we reconstruct the predicted C$α$-only traces into all-atom structures using the cg2all coarse-to-all-atom backmapping method and evaluate their physical and geometric quality with MolProbity. Our model achieves a MolProbity score of 3.034 $\pm$ 0.054, outperforming the evaluated baselines. These results show that a hierarchical flow-matching model with hybrid coordinates can recover global accuracy while retaining local fidelity.
2611.27162.title: Hierarchical Hybrid-Coordinate Flow Matching for Accurate and Physically Plausible Apo-to-Holo Protein Generation

2611.27188.abstract: Grain boundaries (GBs) govern many properties of polycrystalline materials, and inverse design would make the GB structure itself a design variable. Crystal generative models such as MatterGen operate on periodic cells, which contain two GBs. The cell energy defines a single GB only when the two are equivalent, but existing models do not enforce this equivalence. Building on MatterGen, we developed a symmetry-constrained diffusion model in which the two GBs are related by a symmetry operation: atoms near one GB are generated, and those near the other are reconstructed through a symmetry projection applied at every denoising step. We applied it to the $Σ5(210)[001]$ symmetric tilt GB in Al, conditioning generation on the GB energy from a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP). All 350 generated structures kept a geometrically equivalent GB pair after relaxation. Given a target GB energy, the model generated structures at that energy: for the three in-range targets with many nearby training structures, 44% to 70% fell within $\pm 0.1$ J/m$^2$ of the target. Tracking weakened at higher energies and failed outside the training range. Of the 91 near-target structures, 90 matched no training structure under the adopted geometric criterion, indicating that the model can propose configurations near the target energy that are distinct from the training structures, a capability that could help identify unknown metastable GB structures observed in experiments. Building GB-pair equivalence into generation thus makes GB properties well-defined design targets, enabling inverse design of GB structures.
2611.27188.comment: 14 pages, 3 figures; supplementary material included (16 pages, 9 figures, 9 tables); submitted to APL Machine Learning
2611.27188.title: Generating grain boundary structures at a specified energy with a symmetry-constrained diffusion model

2611.27220.abstract: Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure-superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2-xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range-from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T' structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8)shows suppressed Tc (~ 2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin-orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.
2611.27220.title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe2-xTex Polytypic Heterostructures

2611.27303.abstract: Accurate stellar extinction measurements are essential for recovering intrinsic stellar properties and investigating the three-dimensional distribution of interstellar dust. We present reddening estimates for 87,270,425 stars using synthetic SMSS gri photometry derived from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra, combined with Gaia BP and RP, 2MASS JHKs, and WISE W1 photometry. Stellar extinction is determined through empirical SED fitting based on reference stellar loci constructed separately for dwarfs and giants. Comparisons with three external extinction catalogs show good overall agreement, with dispersions of 0.049-0.075 mag in E(B-V). The catalog covers approximately 99.99% of the sky. Using stars with sigma_d/d < 0.2, we further construct reddening maps in four distance ranges from 0 to 5 kpc, revealing prominent molecular clouds and large-scale Galactic dust structures. Extinction-corrected color-absolute-magnitude diagrams show significantly tighter stellar sequences and consistent red-clump features in different Galactic fields. The resulting catalog provides a homogeneous data set for stellar extinction correction and studies of Galactic dust structure.
2611.27303.comment: Accepted for publication in New Astronomy. 11 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables
2611.27303.title: Interstellar extinction estimates for nearly 90 million stars based on synthetic photometry from Gaia XP spectra

2611.27392.abstract: A self-consistent statistical-mechanical theory of the Hall effect in electrolyte solutions is developed by extending the self-consistent Debye-Huckel-Onsager (SCDHO) framework to crossed electric and magnetic fields. The theory incorporates non-local ionic charge distributions through Slater-type form factors and ion-specific coefficients describing the effective Lorentz response, with experimental input for protons and hydroxide ions. Within the random-phase approximation, the Hall conductivity is expressed as mean-field, correlation, and electrophoretic contributions. Both interaction channels include the Lorentz rotation of the complete electric-field-induced ionic velocity. In the point-charge limit with hydrodynamics suppressed, the relaxation correction agrees with independent odd stochastic density functional theory and the relaxation part of Friedman's classical result. For 22 dilute aqueous electrolytes, the mean absolute relative deviations from measured Hall constants and Hall numbers are about 17 percent. At finite concentrations, the theory predicts a nonmonotonic Hall number for NaBPh4 and sign changes of the electrophoretic correction for NaI and HCl. Correlation effects dominate for HCl and LiOH, whereas the two interaction channels become comparable for KOH and aqueous imidazolium salts. The results clarify how ionic mobilities, effective Hall coefficients, charge distributions, and solvent hydrodynamics determine electrolyte magnetotransport.
2611.27392.comment: Published in JCP. Erratum to this paper is accepted for publication in JCP; the corrections are taken into account in present version of the text
2611.27392.title: Hall effect in electrolyte solutions: Self-consistent Debye-Huckel-Onsager theory

2611.27402.abstract: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scale {\it ab initio} calculations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain challenging. We introduce a quantum-classical framework that identifies compact single-particle bases to bring otherwise intractable many-fermion problems within classical reach while preserving an accurate ground-state description. We develop an efficient adaptive search scheme driven by simulated annealing that jointly optimizes natural-orbital-guided transformations and active-space selections. A quantum-assisted ground-state estimator provides search guidance using low-depth circuits and relaxed accuracy requirements, making the framework promising for NISQ devices. We demonstrate the framework's applicability for the nuclear structure of the oxygen isotopes. Our framework opens a new route to tackling complex {\it ab initio} many-fermion problems across disciplines through quantum-assisted basis reduction.
2611.27402.title: Quantum computing for gearing down complex many-fermion problems

2611.27430.abstract: This study presents a novel approach to addressing the limitations in understanding the behavior of charged particles in solutions. The approach is based on the development of the Self-Consistent Debye-Hückel-Onsager (SCDHO) theory, which integrates the effects of non-local charge distributions using a Slater-type charge form factor model. This results in a modified Coulomb potential at short distances, unlike traditional approaches such as the classical Debye-Hückel-Onsager theory. The proposed method relies on explicit expressions derived from gradients of local chemical potentials rooted in classical Density Functional Theory (DFT) and the Ornstein-Zernike formalism for correlation functions. Our theoretical framework enables the derivation of analytic equations that describe both correlation (aka relaxation) and electrophoretic contributions to total electric conductivity. Within the established theoretical framework, the model of smeared charges with Slater-type charge form factors provides an accurate predictive tool that can be applied to a wide range of ion valences, concentrations, and temperatures, including both aqueous and non-aqueous electrolyte solutions.
2611.27430.title: Conductivity of electrolyte solutions: Self-consistent Debye-Hückel-Onsager theory

2611.27444.abstract: Large language models increasingly receive high-level instructions about roles, values, interests, and communication style. Such instructions can conflict even when a prompt assigns them equal authority and provides no priority rule. We study co-authoritative persona conflict, in which a single prompt jointly assigns two opposing personas. Across eight conflict types grounded in published source material and five LLMs, we measure conflict acknowledgment, resolution strategy, and directional stance. Models acknowledge incompatibility in 72% of direct checks but explicitly surface it in only 22% of task responses, revealing silent arbitration. Dominance accounts for 45% of dual-persona responses, and 35% of compromise-labeled responses retain directional lean. Prompt framing further changes the visible form of arbitration substantially more than ordinary paraphrase variation. These findings show that evaluating instruction following should assess whether models disclose conflicts, how they resolve them, and which persona their responses favor.
2611.27444.title: Silent Arbitration: How Large Language Models Resolve Co-Authoritative Conflicting Instructions

2611.27578.abstract: Online batch selection lowers the cost of fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) by replacing each candidate batch with a smaller informative subset. Existing selectors typically depend on a held-out validation or proxy set, or else rely on Euclidean facility-location objectives over unpreconditioned gradients whose diameter-shifted similarities are distorted by heavy-tailed gradient norms and cross-layer anisotropy. We introduce PRISM (Preconditioned Ray-Isotropic Submodular Matching), a validation-free online batch selector that aligns candidate gradients in a factored second-moment metric and casts subset construction as conic facility location over positive ray projections. Computing the required pairwise geometry through factored preconditioned ghost inner products avoids materializing per-example parameter gradients, while the conic objective remains normalized, nonnegative, and monotone submodular---guaranteeing a $(1-1/e)$ greedy approximation whose additive error scales with total batch gradient energy rather than the worst-case outlier diameter. Assigning each candidate to its best-aligned selected ray induces closed-form radial projection weights that automatically shrink orthogonal or noisy examples toward zero. We derive a nonconvex convergence bound showing that optimization error is governed directly by the conic representation cost. Across four LLM fine-tuning configurations spanning 1.5B to 8B parameters, PRISM outperforms full-batch training, Euclidean facility location, and zeroth-order selectors, and rivals or surpasses validation-guided baselines without held-out data.
2611.27578.title: PRISM: Validation-Free Online Batch Selection for LLM Fine-Tuning via Preconditioned Conic Ghost Matching

2611.27580.abstract: Perovskites are promising materials for chemical looping hydrogen production (CLHP) due to their compositional flexibility and tunable redox properties. However, cation substitution opens a vast compositional space, making screening for new high-performing materials computationally demanding. Here, an autonomous active-learning framework combining a Wasserstein autoencoder (WAE) with a deep ensemble surrogate model was used to search for perovskites with a high hydrogen production capacity (HPC). In seven independent runs of 50 cycles, the mean HPC of the acquired compositions rose from 0.41 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$ in the starting set to 2.05 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$, and the best compositions reached 2.65-2.99 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$. All runs enriched Sn on the B-site, mostly combined with Ti and with Mg, Ce, K and Y on the A-site. Twenty diverse candidates (2.22-2.84 mmol H$_2$ g$^{-1}$) were then selected by a multi-objective ranking that also accounts for raw-material price, supply resilience and potential environmental and health impacts. The approach links materials discovery with practical deployment constraints, and the methodology is transferable to other chemical looping processes.
2611.27580.comment: 26 pages, 8 figures, plus 13 pages of Supplementary Information. Code and active-learning databases: https://github.com/stanicic-chalmers/DesigningPerovskitesForCLHP (archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24393271) SQS structures and phonon data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24197403
2611.27580.title: Designing Perovskites for Chemical Looping Hydrogen Production

2611.27583.abstract: Fe-Cr alloys harden at irradiation doses where transmission electron microscopy (TEM) shows no defects, implicating defects too small to be resolved. Their obstacle strength is unknown, so hardening models ignore them and fit measured hardening to visible defects alone. Here, molecular dynamics drives an edge dislocation through relaxed 1-3 nm vacancy and mixed Fe-Cr interstitial clusters in Fe-3Cr, Fe-5Cr and Fe-10Cr at 300 K.
